parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Length, mass and temperature are all SI base quantities.

State **two** other SI base quantities.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The acceleration of free fall $g$ may be determined from an oscillating pendulum using the equation

$$g = \frac{4\pi^2 l}{T^2}$$

where $l$ is the length of the pendulum and $T$ is the period of oscillation.

In an experiment, the measured values for an oscillating pendulum are

$l = 1.50\text{ m} \pm 2\%$
and $T = 2.48\text{ s} \pm 3\%$.
parts.text: Calculate the acceleration of free fall $g$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answers in **(b)(i)** and **(b)(ii)** to determine the absolute uncertainty of the calculated value of $g$.
